routes.label: Lake Shore corridor upgrade
routes.description: Upgrades the existing water-level route (Hudson Line, Empire Corridor, Lake Erie shore) via Albany, Buffalo, Cleveland and Toledo, the path of Amtrak's Lake Shore Limited.

funding.program_name: Corridor Identification and Development Program (Corridor ID)
funding.rationale: Planning entry point: Step 1 scoping is federally funded (about $500K) and places the corridor in the pipeline FRA uses to prioritize FSP-National capital awards. The route spans 5 states (IL, IN, NY, OH, PA), so it needs a multi-state sponsor or interstate compact.

funding.program_name: Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail (National)
funding.rationale: Core federal capital program for intercity passenger rail; this route is an upgrade of an existing rail corridor. Up to 80% federal share. The P50 cost ($25.2B) exceeds RailPlanner's assumed largest single award ($3.0B), so the project would likely need to be phased across several awards. The route spans 5 states (IL, IN, NY, OH, PA), so it needs a multi-state sponsor or interstate compact.

funding.program_name: Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI)
funding.rationale: Fits well: CRISI funds safety, capacity and grade-crossing work on existing lines. RailPlanner assumes awards up to about $250M, so it suits discrete packages such as grade separations or sidings.
Low-interest federal loan that could finance the non-federal match (20% of P50 is $5.0B). Requires a repayment source such as state appropriations or farebox revenue.
Capped at $25M per award (FY2026 notice): useful for a station or grade separation (the route serves 11 stations), not the core build.

funding.program_name: Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail (Northeast Corridor)
funding.rationale: Route reaches New York City, so NEC-adjacent elements (assumed about 5% of cost) could compete for NEC funds.

assumptions: Illustrative estimates: per-mile cost benchmarks are placeholders bracketed by publicly reported US rail projects, not calibrated engineering estimates.
Protected areas and wildlife refuges come from USGS PAD-US (GAP status 1-2); floodplains are an approximate proxy (river corridors plus hand-digitized outlines), not FEMA flood maps.
Population served counts 2020 Census residents within 10 miles of the alignment.
Alignments are conceptual paths on a 1 km grid, not engineered designs. Long corridors follow named alternatives through real corridor cities, with least-cost routing between them.
Cost and schedule come from 5000 Monte Carlo runs per route; P10/P50/P90 are read from TimescaleDB continuous-aggregate histograms (about 1% bin resolution).
Funding program parameters are approximate and change with each funding round.
